D001-D005_h001.question_both:
I’ve been feeling pretty mixed up for… I don’t know, maybe a few months? It’s hard to say exactly. Driving the cab, I lose track of what I’m doing. I’ll be checking the map, then some noise on the street or a random thought just pulls me away, and suddenly I’ve missed a turn or a pickup. Even simple things, like keeping track of the shifts, fuel, payments—I start, then jump to something else and it all ends up in a pile.

I can’t sit still much. Even when I’m waiting at the taxi stand, I’m pacing around, tapping the steering wheel, getting in and out of the car. It’s like my body doesn’t like being idle. I talk a lot with passengers, sometimes I catch myself going on and on and they look uncomfortable, but it’s like I can’t hit the brakes.

Lately, I also get this feeling that people on the street or in the back seat are somehow paying extra attention to me, like they’re judging or talking about me, even when I can’t really hear what they’re saying. I’m not sure if I’m just imagining it, but it makes me uneasy and more distracted when I drive.
D001-D005_h001.question_a:
I’ve always been like this, since I was a kid. My teachers used to complain I couldn’t sit still, always tapping, getting up, talking over others. It never really went away. Even now driving the cab, I feel like I’m wired all the time, like there’s a motor running inside me. I get restless at red lights, fidgeting, drumming on the steering wheel, talking nonstop to customers even when they’re not really in the mood.

I struggle a lot with organizing my day. I double-book rides, forget appointments with my kids, lose track of money I’m supposed to set aside for bills. At home, I start cleaning, then see something on TV or on my phone and suddenly I’m off doing that instead. My mind jumps around; any noise, or even just some random thought, pulls me away from what I’m supposed to be doing.

The strange voices and feeling that the radio is talking about me only started a couple of years ago, after my divorce. But the restlessness, the talking too much, and the distractibility have been there my whole life, long before the weird thoughts began.
D001-D005_h001.question_b:
I’ve been driving a cab in the city for years, and up until about two years ago I was fine keeping track of everything—routes, shifts, bills. Since all this started, my head just feels scrambled. I can’t seem to organize simple things anymore: I’ll start doing my accounts, then halfway through I forget what I was doing, or I’ll double-book fares and mix up times. It’s like my thoughts get hijacked.

Around the same time the other stuff began—hearing people say my name when no one’s there, feeling like some passengers are sending me messages through the radio. Since then, I’m distracted all the time, either by little noises or by these strange ideas that pop in. I lose focus in traffic because I’m caught up in them.

I’ve also become really restless. Even when I’m not driving, I pace around my flat, can’t sit through a TV show. My ex-wife used to tell me I act like I’m constantly revving, like I’m being pushed from inside. And I talk way more than I used to—once I start, I go on and on, jumping from one thing to another, especially about these odd experiences that have been going on.

    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D001-D005_h001.answer_both: B & A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) & Schizophrenia

I guess the main thing is I just can’t seem to keep my head on one thing anymore. At work, I’ll open an email, start to reply, then notice a message pop up, then remember something else, and 20 minutes later I’ve got five half‑finished tasks and nothing actually done. My desk and laptop are a mess of open tabs and random notes; I keep meaning to set up some system, but I get overwhelmed and then just…don’t.

I’m distracted by everything—someone walking past the office door, a sound from the corridor, even my own thoughts. I’ll be in a client meeting and suddenly realize I’ve missed chunks of what they were saying because my mind drifted off.

I move around a lot too. Even on video calls I’m shifting in my chair, pacing when I’m supposed to be “listening,” like I can’t settle. People at work joke that I never sit still. I talk a lot in meetings, sometimes blurting things out before I’ve fully thought them through, and then I worry I’ve come across as rude.

Every now and then, I also get these experiences where I’m not sure if something I’ve heard or briefly seen was really there or just in my head. It doesn’t last long, but it throws me off and makes it even harder to focus. This has been gradually bothering me more over, I’d say, the last few months.
D001-D005_h002.question_a:
Honestly, this has been going on as long as I can remember. Even in primary school, teachers were always on my case because I couldn’t sit still and was constantly talking or blurting things out in class. My parents thought I was just “hyper,” but it never really went away.  

Now, in my 40s, it’s just…different environments, same problems. At work, as an IT consultant, I struggle to keep projects organized. I start one task, then an email pops up or a random thought about something else, and I’m off on that. My desk and inbox are a mess, and I miss small details because my mind jumps around. In meetings, I catch myself talking way too much or interrupting clients, like I can’t hold it back.  

I pace a lot on calls, can’t sit through long sessions, feel like I always need to be moving or doing something.  

The odd thing is, over the last couple of years I’ve also started hearing these faint voices sometimes, like a running commentary. But the restlessness and distraction were there decades before that started; they didn’t change when the voices began.
D001-D005_h002.question_b:

I began hearing this running commentary in my head that doesn’t feel like my own inner voice, like someone muttering about what I’m doing when I’m alone, especially at night. Sometimes I’m convinced people at work are talking about me behind my back, even through the computers. I know that sounds strange, but it feels very real in the moment.

Before all this, I was pretty organized—consulting projects, deadlines, client meetings. But since these odd experiences began, my focus has just fallen apart. I’ll sit down to work on a proposal and get derailed by random thoughts or by the smallest noise; then the voices cut in and I lose my train of thought completely. Now I can’t keep tasks straight, my calendar’s a mess, and projects pile up half-finished.

I also feel constantly agitated, like I can’t sit still. I pace around my apartment or the office, moving from one thing to another, talking a lot—sometimes rambling more than I mean to, especially when I’m feeling watched or judged. All this really seemed to kick in after these strange perceptions started, not earlier in my life.

I find myself wondering if people are talking about me in the restaurant, even when I know that doesn’t really make sense, and it makes it even harder to focus.

I remember being told to “focus” all the time, but my mind would just jump to something else. That’s kind of been the story my whole life.

Now, running several restaurants, it’s a real problem. I’ll start working on inventory, then halfway through I’m answering emails, then I’m in the kitchen rearranging something, and none of it actually gets finished. My desk is a mess of half-started checklists and sticky notes. Even during staff meetings, I catch myself zoning out, thinking about completely unrelated things, then I realize I’ve missed half the conversation and I’m talking over people to catch up.

At first it was just my late husband’s voice, then strangers, like people whispering about me in the hallway or calling my name in the empty rooms I clean. Sometimes I see shadows moving in the corner of my eye, like someone is there, but when I turn, no one’s there.

Since all that began, my mind just doesn’t work the same. I used to keep the apartments I clean in perfect order, had a system and never forgot anything. Now, after the voices started, I can’t seem to organize my tasks. I’ll start changing the sheets, then drift off, staring and thinking about what the voices said, and forget what I was doing. Any little noise or even my own thoughts pull me away from my work.

I feel restless a lot, pacing in my small flat, going from room to room, unable to sit still. When I get anxious about the voices or the feeling that people are watching me, I start talking nonstop, explaining myself to coworkers or to my sister on the phone, jumping from one thing to another. Before all these strange experiences started, I wasn’t like this at all.

I’m always kind of restless. Even when I’m just on my computer, my leg’s bouncing, I’m getting up, pacing around. Friends joke I’m like I’m running on batteries that never run out. When I’m talking, I go on and on, jumping between topics. People have to interrupt me to get a word in.

On top of that, sometimes I feel like my mind isn’t fully lined up with what’s around me. I’ll catch sounds or whispers I’m not sure are real, or feel like there’s something “off” in the background that I can’t quite explain. It doesn’t happen all the time, but when it does, it makes it even harder to focus or finish anything.
D001-D005_h005.question_a:
I’ve always been like this, honestly. My teachers were calling my parents as far back as third grade because I couldn’t sit still, kept talking in class, and never finished assignments unless someone was standing over me. That’s kind of how it still is.

With my editing work now, I really struggle to organize projects. I’ll open up Premiere, have five timelines and ten tabs going, and then get sidetracked by some random thought or a notification. Next thing I know, an hour’s gone and I haven’t touched the actual client brief. Even when I try to plan my day, I bounce from one thing to another and lose track of what I was doing.

I’m constantly fidgeting, pacing around my room between cuts, getting up for no real reason. People tell me I talk nonstop on calls, jump from topic to topic, and interrupt without meaning to. That restless, “motor running” feeling has been there since I was a kid.

The psychotic stuff—hearing a voice sometimes and feeling like people are talking about me online—only started about a year ago. The attention problems and hyper stuff were there long before that and don’t seem to change whether the voices are bad or quiet.

I’ve been having a hard time keeping my mind on things, especially during my shifts. Watching the monitors, I’ll miss something obvious, like not noticing someone tailgating through the gate, or I’ll log the wrong time even though it’s right in front of me. My supervisor’s pointed out a few careless mistakes in the reports lately, and it’s embarrassing because this job is all about paying attention.

Even when I’m just sitting in the booth, my focus “slips.” I’ll start reading an incident report and halfway through I realize I’ve no idea what I just read. At home, it’s the same with the TV—my wife will ask what happened in the show and I can’t really tell her.

I also have trouble just being still. On nights when it’s quiet, I get restless, tap my feet, hum without noticing. My wife complains I can’t just sit and relax, even on weekends. People say I cut them off in conversation; I’ll jump in with what I think they’re going to ask before they finish their sentence, at work and at home.

Lately, on some of those long, quiet shifts, I’ve caught myself thinking I hear someone call my name over the radio when it’s completely silent, or feeling like there’s someone just out of sight in the hallway, even when the cameras show nothing. It doesn’t happen all the time, but when it does, it makes me question whether I’m just tired or if something’s really off. I’m not sure how long this has been building up—it feels like it’s been gradually getting more noticeable over the last few years, but I can’t pinpoint exactly when it started.
D001-D005_h006.question_a:
I’ve always been a bit like this, even as a kid. Teachers used to say I was “bright but scattered,” missing easy points on tests because I’d skip lines or misread questions. My parents said I could never sit still, always fidgeting, talking over people, shouting out answers in class before the teacher finished. That kind of thing has just… never really stopped.

Now I’m 62, working nights as a security guard, and it’s getting harder. Watching the monitors, my mind drifts. I’ll miss something obvious on the screen or fill out an incident report and leave whole sections blank or write the wrong date. My supervisor has pointed out a lot of small, sloppy mistakes. When I try to read the log or a memo, I lose track halfway through and have to start over.

Even at home, I can’t just sit and quietly watch a game or a movie with my wife—I’m up pacing, flipping channels, checking my phone. I interrupt her a lot, answer before she finishes a question.

The strange thoughts and voices only started a couple of years ago. But this restless, distractible way I am—that’s been there my whole life, long before the voices ever showed up.
D001-D005_h006.question_b:

My supervisor has pointed out dumb mistakes I never used to make, like mixing up doors or letting someone in without checking their ID properly. I can’t keep my attention on one screen or one task for more than a few minutes.  

It’s worse when the voices are talking or when I feel like the cameras are somehow watching me back. I get restless then—pacing around the guardroom, fiddling with things, turning the TV or radio on and off. When my wife asks a question, I cut her off and answer before she finishes, like I can’t wait. All this started after the paranoia and hearing voices began; before that, I didn’t have these problems with focus or sitting still.

I’ll be helping my daughter with her homework and I’ll skip parts of the directions or misread them, and then realize later I’d led her totally wrong. I burn food all the time because I think I’ve set the timer, then get distracted and just… lose track. Even simple things, like paying a bill or filling out a school form, I’ll miss a line or write something in the wrong place.

My husband will ask me to do three or four things before he leaves for work—call the pediatrician, switch the laundry, send an email—and by the afternoon I’ve half‑done one and completely forgotten the others. It’s like I start tasks and then they just disappear from my brain.

I can’t sit still; I’m constantly pacing, fiddling with something, jumping up from the table. The kids joke that I move faster than they do, but it doesn’t feel funny. I talk over people without meaning to, cut into my kids’ conversations, finish my husband’s sentences, and he gets annoyed.

What’s scaring me most lately, though, are these moments where I hear someone say my name or a comment, clear as day, and no one’s actually spoken. Sometimes I catch something out of the corner of my eye—like a shadow or someone standing there—and when I look, nothing’s there. It makes me second‑guess myself, like I don’t fully trust my own senses anymore.

Now, at home with the kids, it’s exhausting. I’ll start the dishes, then remember the laundry, then wander off to answer a text, and nothing actually gets finished. My husband gets frustrated because I say I’ll do something—like paying a bill or scheduling an appointment—and I honestly intend to, but it just… disappears from my mind.

I feel like I’m constantly in motion, pacing, fiddling with things, talking too fast. I cut people off in conversation without meaning to; I just blurt out whatever’s in my head.  

The more recent thing—and this is what really scared me—is that in the past year I’ve started hearing a voice sometimes, like someone saying my name when no one’s there, or feeling like the TV is somehow “talking about me.” But these focus and restlessness issues were there long, long before that started.

D001-D005_h025.question_both:
I’ve been struggling for…honestly, I’m not even sure how long now, a few years at least. My wife keeps pointing out that I miss obvious things. I’ll sign off on a contract and later someone in finance finds a stupid mistake I should have caught in the first read-through. It’s not that I don’t know how to do my job; my mind just slips over details, like my eyes are moving faster than my brain.

It’s similar with follow-through. I’ll tell my team we’re going to push a new initiative, I start strong, then it sort of fizzles. Emails go unanswered, tasks half-done. At home, my wife jokes not to give me more than one chore at a time, because I’ll wander off and never finish.

I feel like I’m constantly in motion. Even in board meetings, I’m bouncing my leg, checking my phone, getting up to refill water. People say I pace when I’m on calls. I also cut people off a lot—finish their sentences, jump into conversations before they’re done. It’s gotten worse lately.

On top of that, every now and then, I get these odd experiences—like hearing someone say my name when no one’s there, or being sure people are talking about me at work, even though I can’t prove it. It’s unsettling enough that I’m starting to doubt my own judgment.
D001-D005_h025.question_a:
I’ve always been like this, even as a kid. My teachers used to complain that I’d rush through tests, skip lines, miss obvious stuff. That’s never really gone away. Even now, my assistant has to double-check my emails and contracts because I’ll overlook numbers or send something with obvious mistakes. I start projects at the company with a lot of energy, but I get sidetracked and move on to the next idea before finishing the first. My wife’s been on me for years about half-done home repairs and forgotten errands.

People say I can’t sit still. In meetings, I’m constantly shifting, tapping my foot, checking my phone. My staff jokes I pace like a caged animal. I feel this internal motor going all day, like I can’t just relax on the couch without getting up to “do something.” I also have a bad habit of cutting people off mid-sentence in board meetings, jumping in before they finish, or answering questions before they’re fully asked.

The odd thing is, in the last year or so I’ve also started hearing a man’s voice mumbling my name when no one’s there, and sometimes I’m convinced the news anchors are hinting directly at me. But this new stuff feels separate; the rest of my problems have been there my whole life, long before any of these experiences started.
D001-D005_h025.question_b:
Over the last year and a half, my wife and my board have pushed me to come in. Things started with me feeling like people were watching me—employees, even clients. I’m convinced some of them are planted to spy on me. At home I’ll hear my name being said, almost whispered, when no one’s around. I’ve set up cameras in my office because I’m sure there are bugs in the walls.

What’s changed is that, since all this started, I just can’t stay focused the way I used to. In meetings I’ll lose track of the agenda halfway through and miss obvious numbers on the slides. I’ve sent out emails with ridiculous mistakes, or approved contracts without catching key clauses. My COO will outline a strategy, and I’ll nod, then somehow the plan falls apart because I never actually follow it through—I get sidetracked checking for “evidence” that people are plotting against me.

My wife says I’m constantly pacing, going from room to room at home, and at the office I’m always up, moving, popping into people’s conversations uninvited, cutting them off mid-sentence to ask if they’re talking about me. I wasn’t like this before all the suspiciousness and voices started.
